meta.subtitle: Double-digit growth and rising cash generation at a multiple the market reserves for a business in decline

analystSentiment.commentary:
Intuit's reported numbers and its share price tell opposite stories. FY26 delivered steady growth, a wider operating margin and a step-up in cash generation. Yet at $282.78 the stock sits far below its 52-week high of $689.17 and close to the low of $252.84.

The filing does not explain the decline, and we have no news coverage in our data to explain it either. The 10-K's own risk factors point to where the market's worry likely sits: AI-driven competition, free and low-cost offerings, and government tax software.

We think the current price already discounts a great deal of that risk. On consensus estimates the stock trades on a low-teens forward multiple while returning substantial cash through buybacks and dividends.

We rate INTU BUY with a $300–$380 target range. The case rests on cash flow continuing while the disruption fear stays a fear; the bear case is that the market is right and the earnings base erodes.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Intuit Inc. provides financial management, tax, payments and capital, and marketing products and services, mainly in the United States. Its brands include QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small and mid-market businesses, and TurboTax, Credit Karma and its professional tax software for consumers and tax preparers.

Effective August 1, 2025, the company reported two segments, Global Business Solutions and Consumer, after combining its Consumer, Credit Karma and ProTax businesses. Effective August 1, 2026 it began managing Mailchimp as a separate operating segment. It is headquartered in Mountain View, California.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: The business is growing double digits with expanding margins and very high free cash flow, while the shares trade near their 52-week low. We see the scenario-weighted value meaningfully above the current price (see Valuation), with a bear case that is painful but smaller than the upside. That clears our BUY bar, with the clear caveat that we cannot see the specific news behind the de-rating.

catalysts: Delivery against consensus FY27 revenue and earnings.
Completion of the 2026 reorganization plan and its effect on margins.
First reporting of Mailchimp as a separate segment in fiscal 2027.
Continued share repurchases at a depressed price.
risks: Government-provided tax software competing with TurboTax.
AI-enabled and free competitors eroding pricing or customers.
Fraud, security and privacy incidents on a platform that holds customers' financial data.
An unknown driver behind the share-price decline that the filing does not address.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY26 revenue was $21.4B, up {+13.9%+} from $18.8B in FY25, the fourth straight year of growth between 12.9% and 15.6%. Operating income rose to $5.9B and operating margin widened to 27.4% from 26.1%. Diluted EPS was $16.46, up from $13.67.

Those results absorb a $293 million restructuring charge recorded in FY26 under the 2026 Plan, which management estimates will total approximately $315 million.

Quarterly results are highly seasonal. Tax revenue concentrates from November through April, so the Q4'26 operating margin of 10.9% on revenue of $4.4B reflects the off-season quarter rather than a deterioration.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and short-term investments rose to $4.7B at FY26 year-end from $2.9B. Total debt rose to $7.7B from $6.0B, leaving net debt roughly flat at $3.0B. The current ratio improved to 1.51 from 1.36.

Total equity slipped to $19.0B from $19.7B as capital returned to shareholders exceeded retained earnings. Net debt is modest relative to the year's free cash flow, so the balance sheet does not constrain the company.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose to $8.8B from $6.2B, which management reports as up 42%. Capital expenditure was small at -$175M, so free cash flow reached $8.7B, a 40.4% FCF margin against 32.5% in FY25.

The jump in cash flow outpaced the rise in net income, so part of it may reflect timing in working capital; we would not extrapolate the full FY26 margin. Even at the FY25 margin, the business generates cash well above its dividend and maintenance needs.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $282.78 INTU trades at 17.2x trailing earnings, 11.8x NTM earnings, 10.4x FY28E EPS and 3.5x trailing sales, with a 2.00% dividend yield.

The Street remains positive but split: 34 analysts, 20 Buy, 12 Hold and 2 Sell. The consensus target is $405.60, implying +43.4%, with a median of $400.00 inside a wide range of $290.00–$732.00. That range shows how far apart views on the disruption risk are.

We have no peer multiples to benchmark against, so we judge the multiple against the company's own growth: a low-teens forward multiple is low for a business that has grown revenue double digits for four straight years.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: FY27E revenue of $23.4B and EPS of $23.94 are met, the disruption fear fades, and the multiple recovers to around the level implied by the consensus target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Growth continues near the consensus path toward FY28E EPS of $27.08, buybacks shrink the share count, and the multiple recovers only part of the way toward the consensus target, holding below the Street median.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The market's fear proves right: AI-enabled or government tax offerings take customers or pricing, estimates fall, and the shares break below their 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because the reported trajectory is steady and consensus already embeds a slowdown, to about 9% revenue growth in FY27E. Bull gets more weight than Bear because cash generation and buybacks support the shares even if sentiment stays poor. Bear still gets a quarter of the weight because we cannot see what triggered the de-rating, and the risk factors describe credible ways the earnings base could erode.

The result is a weighted fair value of $332, an expected upside of +17.4% and a bear-case downside of -25.0%.

Our $300–$380 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The FY26 MD&A reports Global Business Solutions revenue of $12.9B, up 16%, and Consumer revenue of $8.6B, up 11%. Global Business Solutions holds QuickBooks and, until fiscal 2027, Mailchimp; Consumer combines TurboTax, Credit Karma and the professional tax products. Service offerings were $18.9 billion, or 88% of total revenue, and management expects that share to grow.

moatFactors.name: Recurring customer relationships
moatFactors.body: The 10-K says the tax businesses depend significantly on customers who return each year, and QuickBooks sits inside small businesses' daily accounting, payroll and payments. That recurrence underpins steady revenue. The same risk factor warns that retaining customers gets harder if they do not see continuing value.

moatFactors.name: Platform breadth and data
moatFactors.body: Intuit spans tax, accounting, payroll, payments, credit and marketing, and it uses consented customer data across the platform to build new offerings. Breadth raises switching costs. It also widens the surface for security, privacy and regulatory risk.

moatFactors.name: Scale in a competitive field
moatFactors.body: The company funds product development and AI investment from very high cash flow. The risk factors are explicit that competitors range from startups to large platforms, and that free and low-cost offerings are increasing.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Recurring relationships and platform breadth have produced years of steady growth and high margins. Durability is now the open question: the company itself names AI-enabled competitors, free offerings and government tax software as threats, and the share price suggests the market believes them. The moat holds if Intuit uses its own AI investment to keep customers rather than letting new entrants reset expectations on price.

points: Consensus expects FY27E revenue of $23.4B, up about 9%, with EPS of $23.94, and FY28E revenue of $25.6B with EPS of $27.08. That is slower revenue growth than FY26 but continued earnings growth.
Services are the growth engine: management expects service revenue to keep rising as a share of total revenue.
The 2026 Plan aims to make the company faster, leaner and more focused, with actions expected to be substantially complete by the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
Mailchimp becomes a separate reportable segment in fiscal 2027, which will show its growth and profitability on their own for the first time in the new structure.
AI is both opportunity and threat: the company is devoting significant resources to it, while warning there is no assurance its AI innovations will be adopted or monetizable.

management.leadership: The captured proxy excerpt covers board independence and related-person policy but does not name the executive officers, so we do not comment on individual executives. Management's main FY26 decision visible in the filing is the 2026 Plan, approved in May 2026, to reduce the full-time workforce and close certain sites while growing technology teams in strategic locations. In our view that is a reasonable response to slower growth, but it carries execution and talent-retention risk the company's own MD&A acknowledges.
management.capitalAllocation:
Intuit returned heavily to shareholders in FY26: share repurchases of -$5.4B, up from -$2.8B, and dividends of -$1.3B. Together they stayed within free cash flow.

Buying back stock near the 52-week low is accretive if the business holds up. Total debt also rose over the year, so part of the return was funded alongside new borrowing. We would rather see buybacks than acquisitions while the shares are depressed.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated November 2025, the Board determined eleven directors and nominees independent under Nasdaq rules: Ms. Burton, Mr. Dalzell, Ms. Liu, Ms. Mawakana, Ms. Nora Johnson, Mr. Norrod, Mr. Prabhu, Mr. Roslansky, Mr. Szkutak, Mr. Vazquez and Mr. Yuan. Independent directors meet in closed session at each regularly scheduled meeting, and the Audit and Risk Committee reviews and pre-approves related-person transactions under a written policy. In our view this is a sound structure. The counterpoint is in the same proxy: the Board deliberately retains longer-tenured directors, and it acknowledges that long tenure can bear on independence from management. These facts predate the FY26 10-K and may have changed.

idiosyncratic: Government tax software: the 10-K warns that federal and state authorities could provide tax software at public expense. The IRS free direct filing system was suspended, but proponents continue to advocate for it, and the legacy IRS Free File Program could expand.

Competition from free, low-cost and AI-enabled offerings: the risk factors describe competitors ranging from startups to large platforms with established consumer user bases, and increasing free and low-cost competition in tax, accounting, payments and personal finance.

Fraud, security and privacy: Intuit holds customers' financial data in industries seeing increasingly sophisticated fraud, including AI-assisted fraud. A major incident would hit trust in the platform directly.
Reorganization execution: workforce reductions and site closures under the 2026 Plan could disrupt product delivery or the retention of the technical talent the strategy depends on.
risks.systemic: Intuit operates in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment with heightened scrutiny across tax, financial services, privacy and AI. Small and mid-market business customers are exposed to the economic cycle, which affects QuickBooks, payments and lending activity. The share price has shown it is exposed to a sector-wide de-rating of software companies seen as vulnerable to AI, independent of reported results.

body: BUY, target range $300–$380. Intuit is still growing, widening margins and generating cash well ahead of its dividend, while the shares trade near their 52-week low.

The main uncertainty is what drove the de-rating, which the filing does not explain. We would turn more cautious if consensus estimates start falling or if government or AI-enabled tax filing gains meaningful adoption; we would add conviction if FY27 results track the consensus path.
